text: Stephen King's It was challenged in Lincoln school libraries in Nebraska in 1987 because of its “corruptive, obscene nature.” In 1992 it was placed on a “closed shelf” at the Franklinville Central High School library in New York because of sexual content, violence, and language, and students needed parental permission to check it out. In Russia, the publisher AST announced that the print run of It had been temporarily pulled from sale to “update labeling requirements.”
